title: Escalate the P1
subtitle: Page, acknowledge, capture
scenario: TKT-4001 escalated. This is a P1 outage - page the right people and capture the acknowledgement so the outage is never sitting unowned. A paged alert with no reply is an incident nobody has picked up.
input: TKT-4001 (outage, P1) routed to escalation. Page the Tier-2 Engineer (the escalation target for outages) and capture their acknowledgement. A P1 also needs the Duty Manager's sign-off. Record who was paged, that they acknowledged, and the duty sign-off.
instructions: Record who the P1 was paged to.
Validate to mint the escalation record.

fields.label: Paged to
fields.explain: Outage P1s escalate to the Tier-2 Engineer - the escalation target - not back to a front-line agent or the queue lead.

fields.label: Acknowledged
fields.explain: A page without an acknowledgement is an outage nobody owns; capturing the ack is the point of the handoff.

fields.label: Duty Manager sign-off
fields.explain: A P1 needs the Duty Manager's sign-off so there is a named owner accountable for the incident.

copilotPrompt: Capture a P1 escalation handoff for TKT-4001: paged to the Tier-2 Engineer, acknowledged yes, Duty Manager sign-off yes. A paged P1 must be acknowledged and owned.
successMessage: P1 escalated and owned. Tier-2 acknowledged and the Duty Manager signed off.

sections.title: Paging is not resolving
sections.body: Sending the page is the start, not the end. The handoff is complete only when someone acknowledges. An unacknowledged P1 is an outage sitting in a channel nobody is watching.

sections.title: The right target
sections.body: Outage P1s go to the Tier-2 Engineer, the defined escalation target - not back to a front-line agent. Paging the wrong person just adds a hop while customers wait.

sections.title: A named accountable owner
sections.body: The Duty Manager sign-off puts a name on the incident. When money and reputation are on the line, 'someone is on it' is not good enough; a specific person owns it.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An escalation record - paged, acknowledged, signed off - that the SLA tracker and digest read.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd page on-call, wait for an 'I've got it', and note the manager who owns the incident before moving on.

takeaway.heading: P1 escalated
points: You paged the Tier-2 Engineer, the defined escalation target.
You captured the acknowledgement, so the P1 is owned, not just sent.
The Duty Manager sign-off names an accountable owner.
The SLA tracker and digest read this escalation record.
The workflow can now escalate a P1 and prove someone owns it.
